label: explain_concept
text:
KV caching speeds up text generation by remembering attention math the model has already done.

A language model writes one token at a time. At each step, attention needs a key vector and a value vector for every token so far. Recomputing those vectors for the whole history would repeat the same work.

The cache stores each token’s key (K) and value (V) after the first computation. For the next token, the model calculates K and V only for that new token and appends them. Attention still sees the full history through the stored vectors.

Generation is much faster. The cost is GPU memory: the cache grows with sequence length, batch size, layers, and attention heads, so long prompts or large batches can fill memory while the model weights themselves still fit.
